ca_cracked_boulder_5.blurb: A small riverside boulder in the Puppy Boulders group at Tuolumne Meadows, high in Yosemite at roughly 8,600 feet. Twelve problems cover the full easy end of the scale: a couple of VB climbs, several V0 and V1 problems, one V2, and a few at V3. Short slab problems line the river side, while the far side holds a taller, harder line that makes a good lead-in to the bigger boulders nearby. The prominent crack up the face gives the boulder its name. It works well as a warm-up stop, and the landings are generally friendly enough for a couple of pads.

ca_lechlinski_crack_formation.blurb: A crack-focused formation in the Queen Valley part of Joshua Tree National Park, off Geology Tour Road. Of its twelve lines, half are trad and five are bolted, with a single boulder problem mixed in. Difficulty starts around 5.7 and the bulk of it sits between 5.8 and 5.11, so there is something for a mid-grade leader and a few tests for stronger climbers. The north face carries thin finger cracks that start hard off the ground. Rubble-pile boulders around its base offer extra problems, and the cracks are the reason to come.

ca_lower_power_station.blurb: A compact roadside crag in the lower Kern River Canyon, reached from Highway 178 just before the first power station when coming up from the east. It holds twelve routes: six bolted lines, four trad climbs and two top-ropes. Grades run from the mid 5.6s through 5.10, with the largest group around 5.10. Older trad lines date from the late seventies, and the sport routes were added later. The stone is crumbly and decomposing in places, so expect some loose texture. There is little standing room at the base, so keep your party small.

ca_alcove_the_4.blurb: A sector of Echo Cliffs in the Santa Monica Mountains, a short climb up and round a corner past the Tower of Zen, about ten to twelve minutes beyond the Grotto. All twelve routes are bolted. The climbing is hard and mostly vertical to slightly overhanging, with holds that run smaller than similar grades elsewhere on the cliff. Seven of the twelve sit at 5.12, a few reach 5.13, and there is just a single 5.10 and one 5.11. The routes shade over in the afternoon, and the right wall also stays shaded in the morning. One of the cliff's three cracks is here.

ca_kim_s_gym_aka_kym_s_gym.blurb: A small bolted sport wall on the Marin coast beside Mickey's Beach, sitting between Steep Ravine and Emperor Boulder. Twelve routes, all sport: a few at 5.8, most clustered around 5.10, and one 5.11. Getting there means a walk past Cobblestone Beach, and the rocks near the waterline are slippery, so low tide and a small swell make for the best visit. Photos show open ocean views from the base. It suits climbers who want a relaxed day of moderate-to-mid-grade leading by the water.

ca_headwall_the.blurb: A steep, overhanging sector high above the Middle Tier of Frustration Creek, in the San Bernardino Mountains along Highway 38. It holds twelve bolted routes ranging from 5.10 to 5.13, with the majority between 5.11 and 5.12, so it is a place for climbers already comfortable on steep rock. Most lines are rated three stars or so, and the best known climbs a pale streak up the middle of the face with a big move through small incuts. Reaching the wall involves scrambling onto a ledge partway up the canyon, so it is not the easy-access part of the creek.

ca_dogma_dome.blurb: A dome above the upper end of Shaver Lake in the western Sierra, off Highway 168 near the Big Creek turn-off. Of its twelve climbs, nine are bolted and three are trad, running from about 5.7 up to 5.11 with the biggest cluster at 5.10. The style is bolted slab, and some lines were bolted on lead, so the older central lines can feel runout. The walk in is short and the setting looks out over the lake. A rack of around ten draws handles most routes, and visitors can expect quiet company.

ca_falls_area.blurb: The main sector of Great Falls Basin, a small desert crag outside Trona on the way toward Death Valley, where a stream once carved through a big plutonic mass. Twelve routes: nine bolted and three trad, from 5.9 up to the 5.11s, with most of the sport lines at 5.11. The area is usually shaded and sits a little past the parking area, reached by working up beside the shady falls, then up a hill and into the second tier. Heat shuts the area down for much of the year, and traffic is light, so loose rock deserves care.
